result.narrative:
Kestrel Marine Parts Ltd sits in the Watch band with a score of 29.9 (PD 0.199), driven entirely by its payment record under the single reporting policy TCI-EX-2026-0001; no news evidence contributes to the score. The buyer has one open overdue invoice totalling $165k exposure ($70k overdue, $95k not yet due) against a $500k limit, so utilisation of the line remains modest even though the payment behaviour itself has worsened over the last two notifications.

The Watch banding reflects a genuine deterioration pattern rather than a one-off blip: the oldest open item is now 38 days past due, versus a prior notification on the same policy that was resolved 12 days late, and notification frequency from this policy has risen from 0 to 2 within the last six months. The adjudicator agreed with the computed band, confirming the zero news contribution is correct (no trusted articles mention this buyer) and that the payment evidence supports a Watch-level rather than High Risk score, while flagging the deteriorating trend as a concern to monitor before any further limit extension.

The recommendation is to maintain the current $500,000 limit with Trade Credit Insurer: the PD of 0.199 is within the 0.25 target and expected loss is unchanged before and after review at $71,640, so no reduction is warranted, but the limit should not be extended further given the open concern.

A move to the lower Healthy band would require the score to fall below 20 (9.9 points lower), which would follow from the current overdue invoice being settled and the DPD trend reversing. Conversely, if the oldest invoice reaches 54 days past due the score would cross into High Risk (50 points, 20.1 away from the current level), at which point the limit should be revisited.
